newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Taiwan sells Jan-Jun'97 fuel oil at $3.5-$4/T.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan sells Jan-Jun'97 fuel oil at $3.5-$4/T.

text.p: Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) has awarded its tender to sell January-June term fuel oil at $3.5-$4 per tonne over Singapore spot quotes, free-on-board Kaohsiung, a company official said on Wednesday.
The tender to sell four to six cargoes of 30,000 tonnes each of 3.0 percent sulphur grade fuel oil for loading in the first six months of 1997 was awarded to a trader, the official said.
CPC started selling high sulphur 180, centistoke fuel oil on a six-monthly term basis since early this year. It has sold about 10 cargoes during the whole of the year in two tenders.
CPC also exports one or two cargoes of 30,00 tonnes each by monthly spot tenders.
In its latest spot tender, CPC sold two cargoes for December 15-27 lifting at around $121 per tonne, fob Kaohsiung.
